title: Multi-fiber photometry in head-fixed mice during spontaneous behavior and dual-cue delay Pavlovian association
author: Safa Bouabid
materials: Conduct two distinct daily sessions during photometry recordings:

steps.title: Prepare Mice for Experiments
steps.instruction: Implement a water restriction and habituation schedule for the mice post-surgery.

substeps.instruction: Three weeks post-surgery, place mice on a water schedule of 1mL water/day, adjusted to maintain 80-85% of initial body weight.

Three to four days before behavior experiments and photometry, habituate mice to head-fixation on a lightweight cylindrical running wheel or a spherical styrofoam treadmill until they run and transition spontaneously between resting and running.

steps.title: Set Up Behavioral Monitoring and Rewards
steps.instruction: Configure the reward delivery system and movement tracking hardware.

substeps.instruction: Install a water spout operated by an electronically controlled solenoid valve, mounted a few mm from the mice's mouths, to dispense 5μL rewards (random inter-trial interval: 10-30 s).
Connect a capacitive touch circuit to the spout to monitor tongue contacts, confirmed with live video of orofacial movements.
For mice on spherical styrofoam treadmills, measure ball rotation in pitch, yaw, and roll using optical computer mice via an acquisition board.
For mice on lightweight cylindrical running wheels, sample linear velocity at 2Khz using a rotary encoder (E2-5000, US Digital) attached to the wheel axle.

steps.title: Perform Behavioral and Photometry Sessions
steps.instruction: Execute the sequential recording and training sessions while performing fluorescence measurements.

substeps.instruction: Session 1: Record photometry during spontaneous behavior on the wheel with no lick spout or reward available.
Session 2: Provide lick spout access and deliver unpredicted 5μL water rewards at random intervals (10-30s).

Pavlovian Conditioning: Present 60 cues daily (30 light, 30 tone) in pseudorandom order. Deliver light cues via a 7 mW LED (20 cm away) and tone cues (12 kHz, 80 dB) via a USB speaker (30 cm away). Present each cue for 6 seconds, delivering a 5μL water reward 3 seconds after cue onset. Use a uniform distribution of 4-40s for the inter-trial interval (ITI) and include eight additional non-contingent rewards per session during ITIs.
Continue training for 26-38 days until cues are associated with rewards.

steps.title: Implement Optogenetic Stimulation
steps.instruction: For unilateral stimulation of DA neurons during unpredicted reward sessions, set up the laser system.

substeps.instruction: Connect implanted optical fibers to a 450 nm laser diode light source (Doric) using a 100 μm patch cord (Doric) with zirconia sleeves.
Calibrate laser power at the fiber tips to 2.5 mW.
Deliver 4 ms blue light pulses at 30 Hz for 500 ms to activate dopamine neurons.
Trigger 5 stimulation trains per session at randomized intervals (excluding unpredicted reward deliveries).

steps.title: Conduct Partial Extinction Phase
steps.instruction: Modify reward probabilities to test cue association.

substeps.instruction: Downshift reward probability for one cue to 20% while maintaining the other at 80%.
Continue training until responses to the 20% cue are significantly reduced.
Reverse the cue probabilities (20% and 80%), counterbalancing the order across mice.

steps.title: Configure Photometry Imaging System
steps.instruction: Set up the custom microscope and camera for fluorescence measurements.

substeps.instruction: Mount the custom-built microscope on a 4’ W x 8’ L x 12’ thick vibration isolation table.
Filter and focus emission light using a bandpass filter and a tube lens onto the CMOS sensor of a Hamamatsu camera.
Connect the microscope to a micromanipulator and mount it on a rotatable arm to position the objective above the mouse head.
Open HCImage Live (Hamamatsu) software.
Perform dual wavelength excitation in quasi-simultaneous externally triggered imaging mode, alternating 470 nm and 570 nm excitation at 36 Hz with 20 ms exposure (18 Hz frame rate per wavelength).
Control TTL pulse timing and duration via custom MATLAB software and a NIDAQ programmable digital acquisition card (National Instruments PCIe 6343).
Transmit voltage pulses from the camera to the NIDAQ after each frame to synchronize imaging and behavioral data.
Record videos of the fiber bundle surface throughout the session.

steps.title: Process and Analyze Fluorescence Data
steps.instruction: Apply post-processing steps to extract and clean the fluorescence signals.

substeps.instruction: Apply motion correction to videos using a whole-frame cross-correlation algorithm.

Extract fluorescence changes from each fiber and the mean fluorescence time series from each region of interest using methods from Vu et al. (2024) and Github repositories BouabidVu2026 and MultifiberProcessing.
Define the baseline by fitting a 2-term exponential function to the mean fluorescence time series.
Normalize fluorescence signals to baseline to calculate ΔF/F signals.
Remove low-frequency artifacts using a finite impulse response high-pass filter: set passband to 0.3 Hz for green sensors (ACh) and 0.1 Hz for red sensors (dopamine).
Note: Skip high-pass filtering for experiments involving optogenetic stimulation of midbrain DA neurons to preserve longer timescale dynamics of ACh signals.
